tier_reason: First-party LiteSpeed blog numbers. The Huffman bench code is public (litespeedtech/benchmarks huffman-decoder/ and huffman-encoder/, Makefile CFLAGS -O3 -DNDEBUG) but no compiler or CPU model is given, and the QPACK ratios are just file sizes of qpackers/qifs encodings from different years that were never re-run. That is C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: QPACK compression ratio on fb-resp.qif (Facebook response trace, 4KB dynamic table): ls-qpack 0.16 vs nghttp3 0.21 when risking blocked streams, 0.18 vs 0.39 with no blocked-stream risk (lower=better; roughly 1.3-2.2x more compact, derived from page data). ls-qpack is also best of the six encoders listed (with qthingey, proxygen, f5, quinn). Shared LiteSpeed HPACK/QPACK Huffman coder (2019 posts, same code as ls-hpack): decoder 1.15-1.96x faster than nginx 1.16.1's decoder; encoder 1.11-2.12x faster than nginx and 1.18-3.59x faster than h2o. It was also 2.37-5.77x faster than nghttp2's 2016 encoder (rev 0e1d0400d86a), but nghttp2 replaced that encoder ('Faster huffman encoding', committed 2019-10-12, nine days after the post), so the nghttp2 figure is stale.
corrections.workload: Huffman encode/decode of four inputs: the string 'LiteSpeed'; a real x-fb-debug header value from the Facebook response QIF; the same value with backslashes inserted to force the slow path; and paragraphs of Jerome K. Jerome's Idle Thoughts. Each loops ~1e6-3.3e8 times, median of 5 runs, with code extracted into litespeedtech/benchmarks. Separately, QPACK compression ratio (compressed bytes / QIF source bytes) on fb-resp.qif from the qpackers/qifs corpus, 4KB table, with and without risking blocked streams. It uses encodings checked into that repo (nghttp3's committed 2019-02-17, ls-qpack's updated through 2019-10-21).
corrections.caveats: All evidence is first-party (LiteSpeed blog). The QPACK comparison measures bytes on the wire, not runtime speed. Its nghttp3 baseline is a draft-era encoding committed to qpackers/qifs on 2019-02-17, about 2 years before the 2021 post and never re-run (nghttp3's lib/nghttp3_qpack.c had ~68 commits between then and the post), while ls-qpack's encodings date from Oct 2019. The Huffman speed numbers belong to the shared LiteSpeed coder: ls-hpack is already catalogued with them, and ls-qpack's lsqpack.c carries the same hencs/hdecs fast-path tables. The 2.37-5.77x vs nghttp2 figure is against a 2016 nghttp2 encoder that nghttp2 replaced on 2019-10-12, so it must not be cited as current. The nginx comparisons still hold: nginx's Huffman code has only been moved and had its logging adjusted since 1.16.1. The bench code is public with -O3, but no compiler or CPU model is stated, so tier C. Benchmark pages: 2021 QPACK post (benchmark_url), https://blog.litespeedtech.com/2019/10/03/fast-huffman-encoder/ and https://blog.litespeedtech.com/2019/09/16/fast-huffman-decoder/.

notes: Every claimed number checks out: encoder figures on the 2019-10-03 post, decoder figures on the 2019-09-16 post, and ratios on the 2021-04-05 post (they also match the qifs file sizes: 57632 and 64477 vs 75201 and 136396 over 351937 bytes). I rated it 'downgrade' at an unchanged tier C because the headline nghttp2 Huffman win is stale and the nghttp3 ratio baseline is a Feb-2019 encoder. benchmark_url now points to the ls-qpack-specific QPACK post. That post measures compression ratio, so the metric field ('throughput') does not match it, and the only runtime-speed evidence is the Huffman coder shared with ls-hpack.

tier_reason: First-party Meta engineering post (2020-10-21) reporting production A/B results for QUIC/HTTP-3 vs HTTP/2 over TCP. It gives no fixed workload, benchmark code, hardware or compiler details, so tier C.

corrections.caveats: First-party production A/B numbers with no fixed workload, hardware, or compiler/flags stated, so tier is capped at C. These are protocol-level wins (QUIC+HTTP/3 with BBR vs TCP+HTTP/2, after retuning app heuristics and flow control), not a measurement of mvfst's code speed. The post itself says mvfst's CPU efficiency was a concern that had to be optimized (GSO, pacing, unacked-data structures), and no comparison against another QUIC stack is made. The baseline is 'HTTP/2 over TCP', not one of the category's named baselines (msquic/quiche/nghttp3), so baseline_in_list=false. The repo has moved to github.com/facebook/mvfst (the facebookincubator URL redirects).

notes: All numbers match the page: 6% fewer request errors, 20% lower tail latency, 5% smaller response headers vs HTTP/2; video MTBR up to 22% better, 8% fewer video errors, 20% fewer stalls; >75% of traffic on QUIC. Metadata checks out: MIT, 1662 stars, last commit 2026-09-26, not archived, not a fork. The GitHub API resolves the repo to facebook/mvfst, so the orchestrator may want to update repo_url.
